role.altitude: The transport electronics repairer keeps tracing faults, talking with crews and writing what was done; photographing and retyping work orders, tracking due dates and searching manuals shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using mobile work orders and page-quoting manual search
role.ambitious_version: A repairer whose records are complete when the job ends.

tasks.short: Write the work order during the job, photograph and mail it to the office, type it into the maintenance system, look up the asset's history, check serial numbers on board, update the on-board logbook, file test reports and calibration certificates, track due dates in a spreadsheet, check records for gaps, discuss records and answer questions to maintain equipment service records.

steps.what: Technician writes the work order during the job: fault, cause, action, parts and hours
Technician photographs the paper work order and mails it to the office
Technician types the work order into the maintenance system against the asset
Technician looks up the asset's service history
Technician checks equipment serial numbers on board against the record
Technician updates the on-board equipment logbook
Technician renames and files test reports and calibration certificates in the asset folder
Technician tracks calibration and test due dates in a spreadsheet
Technician checks records for missing entries before audits
Technician discusses records with the operator's engineer
Technician answers operator questions about past repairs

tasks.design: The technician fills the work order on a tablet during the job, against the asset, with required fields for fault, cause, action, parts and hours; it writes the service record directly, so there is no photo to mail and no retyping. Test reports and certificates are attached in the work order and stored with the asset. The asset record holds calibration and test due dates and sends a notice when one is near, instead of a spreadsheet. Required fields catch most gaps at entry; the audit check stays shorter. History lookups, serial checks, the on-board logbook, discussions and questions stay with the technician. The tablet records jobs, not technician speed, and its use is agreed with the works council.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper work orders were photographed, mailed and retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile work orders against asset records.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a cause that the next technician understands.
tasks.altitude: Less retyping and tracking; the record content stays.

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy offers work orders that fill themselves in, technician checklists and asset management.
AMOS Production records work at the aircraft in real time and stores completed work orders with e-signature.
easyJet reported paperwork processing cut by about 80% after adding e-signature to AMOS; self-reported, no baseline.
Workflow systems and on-board computers that can track staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: maintaining service records; this task carries the record saving for the other tasks in this set.
s1 is the first record of the job and keeps its full time on the tablet; s6 keeps its full time where the operator requires a paper logbook on board.
s2 is gone because no paper order is photographed; s3 keeps 20 for jobs written offline and fixed later.
s7 keeps 40 because the technician still attaches each report; s8 keeps 20 for acting on notices; s9 keeps 60 because judgement on content remains.
The means prior puts 28% in person; the steps show 17%, because record work happens on screens and paper.

incremental.description: Technician keeps checklists and due-date rules current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: about a third of jobs are written offline and fixed later, and audit checks stay long (25.7); high: nearly all jobs on the tablet (32.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search manuals and schematics for the right equipment version, refer to schematics and manufacturers' specifications that show connections, trace circuits on the equipment, phone manufacturer support, discuss with colleagues and note the fault location to locate problems.

steps.what: Technician searches manuals and schematics for the right equipment version

loop.input: The technician's question and the manuals and schematics filed for the asset's model and version.
loop.output: The matching pages, quoted with document and page.
loop.check: The technician opens every quoted page before using it and checks it is for the asset's model and version and shows what was asked; pages that do not fit are searched for by hand.
loop.stop: No answer is given without a quoted page; questions outside the manuals get none.
loop.why_not_simpler: Manuals name the same part in different ways across versions.

steps.what: Technician refers to schematics and specifications that show connections and how to locate problems
Technician traces circuits on the equipment with a meter
Technician phones manufacturer support for missing specifications
Technician discusses the problem with colleagues at the job
Technician notes the fault location

tasks.design: Manuals and schematics are filed by asset model and version, and a question returns the matching pages with document and page, so the technician opens the right page instead of searching binders and folders. Reading schematics, tracing circuits, supplier calls, colleagues and the note stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: The right manual version was found by searching.
tasks.enabler_now: Manuals filed per asset with page-quoting search.
tasks.human_edge: Finding an intermittent fault the schematic does not explain.

reach.learn: Whether the right manual is found first time.

evidence.claim: A search over filed manuals can return matching pages with document and page references.

assumptions: Boundary: reading schematics and specifications; maintaining records (task 11734 in this set) is a separate task.
s6 is the first record of the fault location and keeps its full time; typing the work order is cut in task 11734 in this set.
s1 is priced at 60 because every quoted page is opened and read.
The means prior puts 73% in person; the steps show 60%, because finding and reading documents takes 30%.
research_questions: Is the right manual found first time more often?

incremental.description: Technician files new manual versions to the asset models.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few manuals are filed by model and version yet, so most searches stay in binders and folders (1.2); high: manuals filed for the fleet (5.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the fault report, talk with the driver or crew about symptoms, observe the malfunction with them, phone the customer for details, look up previous faults on the asset and note the fault description to confer with customers to determine the nature of malfunctions.

steps.what: Technician reads the fault report from the operator
Technician confers with the driver or crew about the malfunctions
Technician observes the malfunction with the customer
Technician phones the customer for missing details
Technician looks up previous faults on the asset
Technician notes the fault description

tasks.design: Nothing changes in this task. Understanding a malfunction means talking with the crew and seeing it, and the note is the technician's first record.
tasks.previous_blocker: None; the work is conversation and observation.
tasks.still_hard: Faults that do not show when the technician is there.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the question that makes a driver remember the detail.

evidence.claim: Conferring with crews about faults stays with people.

assumptions: Boundary: conferring with customers; maintaining records (task 11734 in this set) is a separate task.
s6 is the first record of the fault description and keeps its full time; typing the work order is cut in task 11734 in this set.
All steps keep their full time.
The means prior puts 85% in person; the steps show 75%, with 13% on reports and notes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Nothing changes: understanding a malfunction means talking with the crew and seeing it, and the fault note is a first record, so low and high are both 0.
